title: Evaluation labels
description: What an independent reviewer concluded about one case. Authored by a person, never derived from a tool's own output.

reviewKind.description: 'maintainer' means somebody who owns the code said so. A generated case can only ever be labelled by whoever wrote the generator, and calling that maintainer feedback would be claiming a human judgement that never happened.

outcome.description: 'uncertain' is a real answer. It is counted separately and never folded into either side of a rate, because a label nobody is sure of is evidence about the label, not about the tool.

group.description: Cases sharing a group describe the same underlying problem. The agreement rate counts each group once, so one problem cannot be counted three times by being written down three ways. A group is agreed only when every instance in it agreed: a problem the tool missed in one of the ways it appears was not reliably found. Deduplicating therefore lowers a rate or leaves it alone, never raises it.
